newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares on Wednesday finished higher helped by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments that he was hopeful interest rates would be cut before year-end.
Dealers said a late surge in foreign and local interest helped stocks swing into positive territory after the market started weaker as it digested a slew of economic data this week.

"We've seen some quite big foreign and local interest for industrials. I think there is still some underlying bullishness for the industrial board pending a drop in interest rate," James Scott, an equity marketing manager at stockbrokers Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
"We expect a rate cut certainly before the end of the year (from Stals comments). You've seen the reaction on the bond and the equity markets," he added.
The industrial index gained 17.1 points to 9,122.4 points as on of the markets's industrial giants, beer firm South African Breweries climbed 100 cents to finish at 147.25 rand in heavy volume.
"I think guys have thought about all these economic indicators and I think that what Stals said...has worked through everything," one dealer said.
Stals said earlier he was hopeful of a rate cut despite continued high credit growth levels.

Data released on Monday showed June credit extension growth at a much higher-than-expected 16.39 percent from May's 16.65 percent. But money supply and inflation data both slowed strongly, adding impetus to rate cut hopes.
Gold shares ended slightly weaker as bullion, although edging up in the afternoon, yet again failed to breach resistance at $328.
The gold index ended off 4.2 points at 982.6, as the all-shares came down by 0.1 point to close at 7,473.7.

Among the gold shares which took a knock in line with the bullion price were gold mining firms Vaal Reefs and Kloof, which ended 100 cents down at 236.00 rand and 40 cents off at 23.80 rand respectively.

Dealers said overall market turnover was 848 million rand. They expected Thursday's trade to continue in positive mood. In the broader, declining issues otpaced advancing issues by 204 to 190 in a market wich saw 30 shares surge to new highs while 11 sank to new lows.

The South African industrial futures which earlier started steady also followed suit to end firmer after taking a late positive cue from Stals' rate cut comments. A lively local bond market also bouyed sentiment.
The September industrial contract was last at 8,689/700 from 8,640 settlement, golds contract was at 690/700 from 694 settlement and the all-shares contract was at 6,727/40 from 6,718.
